title: Low-temperature magnetism and spin dynamics in the disordered triangular-lattice Yb$^{3+}$ compound LiCaYb$_5$(BO$_3$)$_6$
authors: Monika Jawale, Saikat Nandi, Prashanta K. Mukharjee, Philipp Gegenwart, A. V. Mahajan
abstract: The interplay between geometric frustration, spin--orbit coupling, and structural disorder can give rise to unconventional magnetic ground states in rare-earth triangular-lattice magnets. We report low-temperature magnetic and $^7$Li NMR investigations of the disordered triangular-lattice compound LiCaYb$_5$(BO$_3$)$_6$ (LCYBO). Rietveld refinement confirms a hexagonal $P6_522$ structure with partial Ca/Yb antisite disorder and fractional Li occupancy. Magnetic susceptibility and magnetization measurements indicate a well-isolated effective $J_{\mathrm{eff}}=1/2$ Kramers doublet with weak antiferromagnetic interactions ($θ_{\mathrm{CW}} \approx -0.54$~K). The specific heat reveals a weak anomaly near 0.43 K, suggesting the development of short-range correlated magnetism rather than conventional long-range order. $^7$Li NMR spectra broaden strongly upon cooling, consistent with increasingly inhomogeneous internal magnetic fields. The spin-lattice relaxation exhibits two relaxation components consistent with disorder-induced distributions of local magnetic environments arising from antisite disorder and competing exchange pathways. Our results establish LCYBO as a structurally disordered frustrated triangular-lattice magnet with correlated low-energy spin dynamics.
summary: This work characterizes the magnetic behavior of the disordered triangular-lattice magnet $	ext{LiCaYb}_5(	ext{BO}_3)_6$. By combining magnetic susceptibility, specific heat, and ${}^{7}	ext{Li}$ NMR measurements, the authors show that the system enters a correlated, low-energy spin dynamic regime. The findings highlight how structural disorder and geometric frustration suppress conventional magnetic ordering, establishing it as a model disordered frustrated magnet.
main_problem: The study investigates the low-temperature magnetism and spin dynamics in a geometrically frustrated, disordered triangular-lattice rare-earth magnet.
main_result: The compound exhibits correlated low-energy spin dynamics characterized by a well-isolated effective $J_{	ext{eff}}=1/2$ Kramers doublet, suggesting a correlated magnetic state rather than conventional long-range order.
method: A combination of bulk measurements (magnetization, specific heat) and local probes (${}^{7}	ext{Li}$ NMR) was employed to characterize the magnetic ground state.
model_or_system: The system is $	ext{LiCaYb}_5(	ext{BO}_3)_6$, a rare-earth magnet with $	ext{Yb}^{3+}$ ions forming a triangular lattice. The physics is complicated by geometric frustration, strong spin-orbit coupling, and structural disorder (antisite mixing and vacancies).
key_observables: Magnetic susceptibility ($\chi(T)$), specific heat anomaly ($T^* \approx 0.43 	ext{ K}$), ${}^{7}	ext{Li}$ NMR linewidth broadening, and spin-lattice relaxation components.
important_parameters: Effective $J_{	ext{eff}}=1/2$ doublet, weak antiferromagnetic interaction ($	heta_{	ext{CW}} \approx -0.54 	ext{ K}$), and a large Crystal Electric Field (CEF) gap ($\Delta_{	ext{CEF}} \approx 200 	ext{ K}$).
main_assumptions: The low-energy physics can be effectively described by spin-$1/2$ Kramers doublets due to strong SOC/CEF effects.
figures_summary: The notes mention figures illustrating the refined crystal structure and powder XRD patterns confirming single-phase crystallization.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first characterizing the structure and disorder, then measuring bulk magnetic properties ($\chi, C_p$) to establish the effective low-energy spin model, and finally using local probes (${}^{7}	ext{Li}$ NMR) to map out the inhomogeneous spin dynamics.
why_interesting: The combination of geometric frustration, disorder, and strong spin-orbit coupling places this material in a highly relevant regime for studying quantum disordered magnetism, which shares conceptual links with frustrated quantum magnets studied in AMO physics.
